11: 
12: # GKE Observability
13: 
14: This reference covers monitoring, logging, and metrics configuration for GKE.
15: The golden path enables comprehensive observability including control-plane
16: metrics.
17: 
18: > **MCP Tools:** `get_cluster`, `list_k8s_events`, `get_k8s_logs`,
19: > `get_k8s_cluster_info`, `describe_k8s_resource`. **CLI-only:** `gcloud
20: > container clusters update --monitoring=...`, `gcloud logging read`
21: 
22: ## Golden Path Observability Defaults
23: 
24: Setting                                             | Golden Path Value                                                                                                                                   | Notes
25: --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -----
26: `loggingConfig` components                          | SYSTEM_COMPONENTS, WORKLOADS                                                                                                                        | Full workload logging
27: `monitoringConfig` components                       | SYSTEM_COMPONENTS, STORAGE, POD, DEPLOYMENT, STATEFULSET, DAEMONSET, HPA, JOBSET, CADVISOR, KUBELET, DCGM, APISERVER, SCHEDULER, CONTROLLER_MANAGER | Full suite including control-plane
28: `managedPrometheusConfig.enabled`                   | `true`                                                                                                                                              | Google-managed Prometheus
29: `advancedDatapathObservabilityConfig.enableMetrics` | `true`                                                                                                                                              | Dataplane V2 flow metrics
30: `loggingService`                                    | `logging.googleapis.com/kubernetes`                                                                                                                 | Cloud Logging
31: `monitoringService`                                 | `monitoring.googleapis.com/kubernetes`                                                                                                              | Cloud Monitoring
32: 
33: ### Control-Plane Metrics (Golden Path Addition)
34: 
35: The golden path adds three control-plane monitoring components not present in
36: default clusters:
37: 
38: | Component            | What It Monitors                                                       |
39: | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
40: | `APISERVER`          | API server request latency, error rates, admission webhook performance |
41: | `SCHEDULER`          | Scheduling latency, pending pods, scheduling failures                  |
42: | `CONTROLLER_MANAGER` | Controller work queue depth, reconciliation latency                    |
43: 
44: These are critical for diagnosing cluster-level issues (slow API responses,
45: scheduling delays, stuck controllers).
46: 
47: ## Enabling Full Monitoring
48: 
49: **Say this whenever you hand over a `--monitoring` command:**
50: 
51: 1.  **Control-plane metrics are NOT enabled by default.** State this outright in
52:     your answer — do not leave it implied by the fact that you are supplying an
53:     enable command. `API_SERVER`, `SCHEDULER`, and `CONTROLLER_MANAGER` are off
54:     on every new cluster and collect nothing until explicitly turned on, and the
55:     same is true of `DCGM`, `CADVISOR`, `KUBELET`, and kube-state (`POD`,
56:     `DEPLOYMENT`, `STATEFULSET`, `DAEMONSET`, `HPA`, `STORAGE`, `JOBSET`).
57:     `SYSTEM` is the only package on by default. A user asking "why are there no
58:     API server metrics" has almost always simply never enabled them.
59: 2.  **The flag replaces, it does not append.** The set supplied to `--monitoring`
60:     overrides the previous setting entirely, so omitting a component silently
61:     turns it off. Always pass the full desired list, and always include `SYSTEM`
62:     — it cannot be disabled while monitoring is on, and never on Autopilot.
63: 3.  **These metrics bill per sample ingested** via Managed Service for
64:     Prometheus. Enabling the full suite on a large cluster is a real cost
65:     increase; mention it rather than presenting the list as free.
66: 
67: > **The gcloud flag and the API field use different spellings for the same
68: > components.** Do not copy names between them:
69: >
70: > Component        | `gcloud --monitoring=` | `monitoringConfig` API enum
71: > ---------------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------------
72: > System           | `SYSTEM`               | `SYSTEM_COMPONENTS`
73: > API server       | `API_SERVER`           | `APISERVER`
74: > Controller mgr   | `CONTROLLER_MANAGER`   | `CONTROLLER_MANAGER`
75: >
76: > The remaining components share a spelling. Using an API enum in the CLI flag
77: > (or the reverse) fails the command — this is a common and confusing error.
78: 
79: ```bash
80: # Enable golden path monitoring suite
81: gcloud container clusters update <CLUSTER_NAME> --region <REGION> \
82:   --monitoring=SYSTEM,API_SERVER,SCHEDULER,CONTROLLER_MANAGER,STORAGE,POD,DEPLOYMENT,STATEFULSET,DAEMONSET,HPA,JOBSET,CADVISOR,KUBELET,DCGM \
83:   --quiet
84: 
85: # Enable Managed Prometheus
86: gcloud container clusters update <CLUSTER_NAME> --region <REGION> \
87:   --enable-managed-prometheus \
88:   --quiet
89: 
90: # Enable Dataplane V2 observability metrics
91: gcloud container clusters update <CLUSTER_NAME> --region <REGION> \
92:   --enable-dataplane-v2-flow-observability \
93:   --quiet
94: ```
95: 
96: ## Managed Prometheus
97: 
98: Golden path enables Google Managed Prometheus for metrics collection and
99: querying.
100: 
101: **Querying metrics:**
102: 
103: -   Use Cloud Monitoring Metrics Explorer in the console
104: -   Use PromQL via the Prometheus UI or API
105: -   Grafana dashboards via Managed Grafana
106: 
107: **Key GKE metrics:**
108: 
109: | Metric                                            | Source             | Use                    |
110: | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------- |
111: | `container_cpu_usage_seconds_total`                | cAdvisor           | Pod CPU usage          |
112: | `container_memory_working_set_bytes`               | cAdvisor           | Pod memory usage       |
113: | `kube_pod_status_phase`                            | kube-state-metrics | Pod lifecycle          |
114: | `apiserver_request_duration_seconds`               | API Server         | Control plane latency  |
115: | `scheduler_scheduling_attempt_duration_seconds`    | Scheduler          | Scheduling performance |
116: | `kubernetes.io/node/cpu/core_usage_time`           | Cloud Monitoring   | Node CPU               |
117: | `DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL`                             | DCGM               | GPU utilization        |
118: 
119: ## Live Resource Usage (kubectl-only)
120: 
121: No MCP or gcloud equivalent exists for live resource usage. Use `kubectl top`:
122: 
123: ```bash
124: kubectl top pods --all-namespaces --sort-by=cpu
125: kubectl top nodes
126: kubectl top pods --containers -n <NAMESPACE>  # per-container breakdown
127: ```
128: 
129: ## Cloud Logging (gcloud-only)
130: 
131: **Querying cluster logs** (no MCP equivalent — use `gcloud logging read`):
132: 
133: ```bash
134: # System component logs
135: gcloud logging read \
136:   'resource.type="k8s_cluster" AND resource.labels.cluster_name="<CLUSTER_NAME>"' \
137:   --project <PROJECT_ID> --limit 50 \
138:   --quiet
139: 
140: # Workload logs for a specific namespace
141: gcloud logging read \
142:   'resource.type="k8s_container" AND resource.labels.cluster_name="<CLUSTER_NAME>" AND resource.labels.namespace_name="<NAMESPACE>"' \
143:   --project <PROJECT_ID> --limit 50 \
144:   --quiet
145: 
146: # Audit logs (who did what)
147: gcloud logging read \
148:   'resource.type="k8s_cluster" AND logName:"cloudaudit.googleapis.com"' \
149:   --project <PROJECT_ID> --limit 50 \
150:   --quiet
151: ```
152: 
153: ## Diagnostic Settings
154: 
155: For security monitoring and troubleshooting, enable control-plane audit logs:
156: 
157: ```bash
158: # View current logging config
159: gcloud container clusters describe <CLUSTER_NAME> --region <REGION> \
160:   --format="yaml(loggingConfig)" \
161:   --quiet
162: ```
163: 
164: ## Alerting
165: 
166: Set up alerts for critical conditions:
167: 
168: Condition               | Metric                                              | Threshold
169: ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------
170: High API server latency | `apiserver_request_duration_seconds`                | P99 > 5s
171: Pod crash loops         | `kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total`          | > 5 in 10min
172: Node not ready          | `kube_node_status_condition`                        | condition=Ready, status!=True
173: High GPU utilization    | `DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL`                              | > 95% sustained
174: PVC near capacity       | `kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes / capacity`        | > 85%
175: Scheduling failures     | `scheduler_schedule_attempts_total{result="error"}` | > 0
176: 
177: > **Prerequisite:** The `kube_*` series above (e.g., `kube_pod_status_phase`,
178: > `kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total`, `kube_node_status_condition`)
179: > come from **kube-state-metrics**, which GKE does not collect by default.
180: > Deploy the Managed Prometheus kube-state-metrics package first.
181: 
182: ### Proposing Dashboards & Alerts (Production Rules)
183: 
184: When designing or proposing alerting and dashboard strategies for GKE:
185: 
186: 1.  **Always explicitly name Google Cloud Monitoring** as the platform to
187:     implement these alerts and dashboards.
188: 2.  **Always include API server latency** (via
189:     `apiserver_request_duration_seconds` metric) on the dashboard as a critical
190:     indicator of control plane health, alongside node CPU/Memory and pod crash
191:     loops.
192: 
193: ### Node Health (Production Rules)
194: 
195: A comprehensive assessment of node health relies on analyzing these two metrics together:
196: 
197: 1.  **`kubernetes.io/node/status_condition`** (filtered by `status_condition="Ready"`): Use this to track healthy nodes. Note that it will only report values for nodes that have successfully bootstrapped.
198: 2.  **`compute.googleapis.com/instance_group/size`** (filtered by `instance_group_name="gke-<cluster_name>-.*"`): Use this to track the total number of nodes in a specific cluster. Note that it does not differentiate between healthy and unhealthy nodes.
199: 
200: ## Cost Considerations
201: 
202: Monitoring and logging have associated costs:
203: 
204: -   **Cloud Logging**: Charged per GiB ingested beyond free tier (50
205:     GiB/project/month)
206: -   **Cloud Monitoring**: Free for GKE system metrics; custom metrics charged
207:     per time series
208: -   **Managed Prometheus**: Charged per samples ingested
209: 
210: To reduce costs in non-production:
211: 
212: ```bash
213: # Reduce to system-only monitoring
214: gcloud container clusters update <CLUSTER_NAME> --region <REGION> \
215:   --monitoring=SYSTEM \
216:   --quiet
217: ```
218: 
219: ## Distributed Tracing & Continuous Profiling (Recommended)
220: 
221: **Not golden path defaults** — recommended for production microservice
222: architectures and performance-sensitive workloads.
223: 
224: -   **Cloud Trace**: Add OpenTelemetry SDK to your app with the
225:     `opentelemetry-operations-go` (or equivalent) exporter. Traces appear in
226:     Cloud Trace console. Identifies cross-service latency bottlenecks.
227: -   **Cloud Profiler**: Add the Cloud Profiler agent to your app. Profiles CPU
228:     and memory usage in production with low overhead. Identifies hotspots and
229:     compares across versions.
230: 
231: **Recent additions:**
232: 
233: -   **Managed OpenTelemetry for GKE (Preview)**: Managed in-cluster OTLP
234:     endpoint plus auto-instrumentation for traces, metrics, and logs. Requires
235:     GKE 1.34.1-gke.2178000+; enable with `gcloud beta container clusters
236:     update ... --managed-otel-scope=COLLECTION_AND_INSTRUMENTATION_COMPONENTS`.
237: -   **PSI (Pressure Stall Information) metrics**: cAdvisor
238:     `container_pressure_{cpu,memory,io}_{waiting,stalled}_seconds_total` series
239:     (beta in Kubernetes 1.34) can be collected via a Managed Prometheus
240:     `ClusterNodeMonitoring` resource; GKE's documented collection path requires
241:     GKE 1.35+.
242: 
243: ## LQL Query Examples
244: 
245: Common Logging Query Language patterns for GKE troubleshooting:
246: 
247: ```
248: # Error logs for a specific container
249: resource.type="k8s_container" AND resource.labels.container_name="my-app" AND severity>=ERROR
250: 
251: # OOMKilled events
252: resource.type="k8s_event" AND jsonPayload.reason="OOMKilling"
253: 
254: # Pod scheduling failures
255: resource.type="k8s_event" AND jsonPayload.reason="FailedScheduling"
256: 
257: # Audit logs (who did what)
258: resource.type="k8s_cluster" AND logName:"cloudaudit.googleapis.com"
259: ```
260: 
261: ## Supporting Links
262: 
263: -   [GKE system metrics](https://docs.cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/metrics_kubernetes)
264: -   [GKE Observability Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/observability)
265: -   [Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus](https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/managed-prometheus)
266: -   [Cloud Logging Query Language (LQL)](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/view/logging-query-language)
267: -   [Google Cloud Monitoring Alerts](https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/alerts)"}}
